newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RTZ says upbeat about int'l economic outlook.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RTZ says upbeat about int'l economic outlook.

text.p: International mining house RTZ Corp-CRA Ltd said it was reasonably confident about the international economic outlook, with an improvement helping iron ore sales in the second half of calendar 1996.
"As a matter of fact we are reasonably upbeat about '97," chief executive Robert Wilson told analysts at a briefing for the first half results.
"Because looking at the economic trends we think that the United States might well slow down in '97 .... but the other main economic areas are likely to improve," Wilson said.
He would not forecast full year profits for the miner.
Asked about the outlook for iron ore sales from the Hamersley operations in Australia during the second half of calendar 1996, Wilson said the market should improve.

First half net profit from the iron ore division fell to A$133 million from A$170 million while sales eased to A$583 million from A$609 million, with the company saying lower demand in Europe and Japan was offset by firmer Asian shipments, particularly to China.
"The first half of this year for iron ore sales has been quite depressed with very poor market conditions in Japan and Europe," he said.
"As we go into the second half year we are expecting to see some recovery in both areas, both in Western Europe as a whole and Japan," Wilson said.
"There is nothing very dramatic happening in either of these economic areas but we do see improvement from what we have seen in the first half of this year," he said.
